{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is neutral or negative (sentiment ≤ 0.00) to counteract overconfidence in upward moves.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility in early periods (e.g., first 5 days) when price is trending downward — avoid overreacting to short-term noise.",
    "When true outcome spikes sharply (e.g., >10% from prior day), reduce forecast overshoot by 10–20% to prevent overcorrection.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.25).",
    "In late periods (e.g., last 5 days of forecast horizon), increase downward bias if sentiment is neutral or negative — prices often consolidate or reverse.",
    "If sentiment is positive (>0.25) and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast by 5–10% to capture momentum — but cap at 15% to avoid overextension.",
    "Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when history shows strong downward momentum (e.g., last 3 days < 60.00) — reduce forecast by 5–10% unless sentiment is strong."
  ]
}
